propositions: Fixed-count threshold compaction (control T=10) writes complete full-state snapshots and retains all prior ones append-only, causing retained-snapshot bytes to grow superlinearly Θ(N²) as state size S grows.

Geometric and byte/replay-cost-aware cadence policies reduce retained-snapshot bytes to Θ(N) linear growth while bounding replayed bytes to a tunable fraction of snapshot size, measured at 344× reduction (N=8,000).

All candidate cadence policies preserve ADR 0035 invariants (conservative fold horizon, rebuild-on-stray, crash recovery, rollback, two-clone union safety) because they change only the WHEN-to-fold trigger, not snapshot placement or source-event retention.

Byte/replay-cost-aware cadence with alpha parameter (fold when pending_source_bytes >= alpha * active_snapshot_bytes) bounds read cost to (1+alpha)× of unavoidable snapshot load while tuning amplification factor to 1/alpha of live state.

Implementation requires a new config key compact.snapshot_alpha with default ≤0 for backward compatibility, and a dedicated two-clone reconvergence test, deferred to a separate ADR and follow-up ticket.
